text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Monday.

- A memorial to the victims of World War One and Two is ravaged by vandals on the Ulrichsberg, in the southern province of Carinthia. Police found a letter claiming responsibility from a group called "Kommando Z.A.L.A".
- Among the 700,000 Poles, Czechs, Hungarians and Slovaks wanting to emigrate, 150,000 want to come to Austria.
- Prices for new cars slip dramatically.
- Austria sold around 12.5 billion schillings of wood in 1996, making it the country's second provider of foreign currency after tourism.
- Conservative People's Party head Wolfgang Schuessel dashes union and workers' hopes by saying the budget must stand as it is, that no savings measures will be alleviated.

- Freedom Party head Joerg Haider wants a referendum on the the introduction of the euro. He is also considering nominating his own candidate for next year's presidential elections should the incumbent president's programme not suit him.
- The High Court in London has fined VA Industries U.K. Ltd, the British subsidiary of VA Tech unit VAI, 2.7 million schillings for "serious" disregard of the court.
